title: Audit policy precedence conflict — GPO console vs. live auditpol output
event_type: Advanced Audit Policy Configuration, Logon subcategory, GPO editor display vs. `auditpol /get /category:*` on the same host

fields.label: GPO Editor Display (Advanced Audit Policy Configuration)

callouts.field_label: GPO Editor Display (Advanced Audit Policy Configuration)
callouts.explanation: This is what an admin sees in the GPO console and reasonably trusts — it says the Logon subcategory is auditing Success events.
The actual, currently-enforced state on the host itself, queried live — shows No Auditing, meaning zero logon events are actually being recorded despite the GPO console's claim.
Because this value isn't set to force advanced-policy precedence, the legacy basic audit policy silently wins the conflict and overrides the advanced subcategory setting shown in the GPO editor.

note: Conceptual/illustrative field breakdown of the audit-policy precedence conflict described in the Engineering Reality box; not a captured screenshot of any product interface.
